headline: Mangroves gain ground globally, marking turnaround after decades of loss
meta_description: After decades of decline, mangrove forests are expanding worldwide, signaling a major environmental victory for coastal ecosystems.
summary_short: Mangrove forests are staging a comeback globally after years of steady loss, marking a rare environmental turnaround for these vital coastal ecosystems.
body:
Mangrove forests are experiencing a global expansion after decades of steady decline, signaling a major shift in coastal ecosystem recovery. This turnaround represents one of the few bright spots in environmental restoration efforts worldwide, as these resilient trees reclaim ground lost over generations.

Mangroves have long faced intense pressure from development, aquaculture, and coastal conversion. Their recovery now demonstrates that focused conservation efforts can reverse even deeply entrenched environmental losses. These forests play a crucial role in protecting coastlines, sequestering carbon, and supporting marine biodiversity—making their resurgence significant for both climate and nature.

The global momentum behind mangrove restoration reflects growing recognition of their ecological importance. Communities and conservation organizations are increasingly prioritizing their protection and replanting, transforming what seemed like inevitable decline into genuine hope for these ancient forests.
quick_facts: Coastal forests expanding in multiple regions worldwide
Ecosystems vital for carbon storage and marine life
Conservation efforts successfully restoring lost ground
